original: This is a critical narrative review. Its question is what routine cine CMR can establish about regional myocardial motion and strain, so the literature was assembled to cover the estimator families, the validation targets and the public resources that bear on that question; it does not enumerate every cine strain study. The corpus was built in three steps. The first step began from a core set of papers, listed in the Supplementary Methods, and followed their reference lists and citing articles; guideline, dataset and repository records were added by hand because bibliographic databases index them incompletely; expansion stopped when a further round changed no method family, comparison axis or principal conclusion.
revision: This critical narrative review asks what routine cine CMR can establish about regional myocardial motion and strain. It combines selected method papers, empirical comparisons, reviews and public-resource descriptions; it is not a systematic review or a census of cine-strain studies. The supplied search history describes citation expansion from a core set and a structured search of PubMed, Europe PMC and OpenAlex executed on 3 September 2026, with a publication cutoff of 1 September 2026 and a cap of 100 records per query. The six query families concerned regional strain after infarction, known-motion validation, prior perturbation, conditional recoverability, failure-aware prediction and regional localisation or attenuation. The surviving query log records 18 query--database combinations; the original record exports and record-level screening file are unavailable in the supplied package.
rationale: 如实说明历史记录和缺失文件，不重新认证历史程序

original: The second step was a structured search of PubMed, Europe PMC and OpenAlex, with a publication cutoff of 1 September 2026, built from six concepts: regional cine strain after infarction, known-motion or digital-phantom validation, perturbation of the prior or regularisation, conditional recoverability (whether a regional abnormality can be recovered under stated acquisition and estimator conditions), failure-aware or selective prediction, and regional localisation, spillover and attenuation. The purpose of that search was to find any study that combined a prescribed regional abnormality, known motion and a controlled change of the estimator, and to collect the studies that address part of that design. Records were screened on title and abstract against this purpose, and each retained record that supports a statement in the review was then read at the depth recorded in the evidence ledger. The third step, completed on 8 October 2026, re-verified the central primary studies, the dataset descriptions and the bibliographic metadata of every reference against PubMed/PMC, publisher pages, Crossref or DataCite records and official dataset pages, and read the reviews published from 2024 to 2026, which also formed part of the core set, so that this review could be positioned against them.
revision: The historical notes describe a single software-assisted title-and-abstract screening pass, followed by a directed check on 9 September under the same cutoff. Their deduplication, retention counts and thematic stopping rule cannot be reconstructed from the surviving records. A separate October update added or rechecked sources, including publications after the September cutoff; the supplied narrative dates that pass to 8 October, whereas its metadata ledger is dated 9 October. On 11 October 2026, the present author-review revision rechecked central quantitative claims against primary-source methods, results and tables, and corrected their interpretation. This targeted verification is documented separately in the Supplementary Methods and evidence addendum; it does not reconstruct the historical search or establish exhaustive coverage.

original: Three limits follow from this design. The structured search is bounded by its query strings, its three databases and a cap of 100 records per query, so the statements in \cref{sec:registration} and \cref{sec:knownmotion} that no study of a given kind was identified hold within that boundary. Screening was performed in a single pass with software assistance for query execution, deduplication and screening suggestions (see Declarations); it was not repeated by a second reviewer, no record was excluded on full-text criteria, and the retention decisions are the author's responsibility. Reading depth depends on the role a source plays: the primary studies on which the principal conclusions rest were read in full; part of the method-lineage and reconstruction literature was read at abstract level, and an abstract-level reading supports only the study design and the results stated in the abstract. The evidence ledger states the depth for every cited source, and Supplementary Table~S3 marks the entries read at abstract level. The query strings, hit counts and screening record are given in the Supplementary Methods.
revision: Reading depth varies by source. Central comparisons were checked in the relevant full-text sections where accessible; other method-lineage entries rely on abstracts or bibliographic records and support only the information available at that depth. The updated evidence tables distinguish those readings from inherited extraction notes and failed access. Missing detail in a retrieved abstract is not evidence that the original study omitted an experiment. Accordingly, the review identifies priorities for focal validation without claiming that a design is absent from the entire literature. Historical counts and the limits of their auditability are retained in the Supplementary Methods.

original: These three factors come apart in practice, and the way they come apart is the basis of an attribution experiment. Suppose a focal deficit is under-recovered. If the same estimator recovers it when \(\alpha\) is reduced, the limitation was the estimation process. If it is still under-recovered after the known deficit has been projected directly onto the estimator's function space (a cheap test that uses the known field in place of the images), the limitation lies in the representation. If neither holds, and the deficit becomes recoverable when the same motion is re-imaged at finer resolution or with added long-axis views, the limitation lay in the acquired input. That last attribution is conditional, because a finer acquisition also changes discretisation, optimisation conditioning and, for a learned estimator, the training distribution, so the estimator, representation and training regime must be held fixed for it to hold. In every case, attributing an observed regional error requires an experiment that holds the other two factors fixed. \Cref{sec:threequestions} returns to this separation when reconciling discordant results, and the known-motion resources in \cref{sec:resources} are the setting in which the experiment can be run.
revision: Controlled tests can help distinguish these contributions, although they can coexist. Recovery after reducing a regularisation weight implicates the estimation process under that comparison; it does not establish that the input uniquely determines the motion. A representation test should fit the known displacement directly in the candidate function space, stating the norm, boundary conditions and sampling, and then measure error in both displacement and the specified strain or abnormality attribute. A small displacement approximation error need not imply a small derivative error. Re-imaging the same motion at finer resolution or with additional views can test sensitivity to input information, but also changes discretisation, optimisation and potentially the training domain. Such comparisons need matched controls, including retraining when a training-loss weight is changed. These are diagnostic experiments, not mutually exclusive causal assignments. \Cref{sec:threequestions} returns to their interpretation, and \cref{sec:resources} describes resources on which they could be performed.
rationale: 允许因素耦合并定义投影/导数误差，保持前瞻性质

original: The same supervision route has since been extended. Lei and colleagues report a DENSE-supervised network for routine bSSFP cine that estimates large myocardial rotation in a separate time-series branch and radial motion by deformable registration in a second, motivated by the observation that earlier DENSE-supervised models captured twist and torsion poorly~\cite{lei2025denserotation}. revision: The same supervision route has since been extended. Lei and colleagues describe a DENSE-supervised model with separate myocardial-rotation and radial-motion branches for routine bSSFP cine; the retrieved abstract motivates this design by difficulty recovering large rotation~\cite{lei2025denserotation}. MyoNet takes a related approach in Dahl salt-sensitive rats with radiation-induced injury. Cine segmentations are converted to binary spatiotemporal inputs, and displacement supervision is obtained by applying sine-wave modelling (SinMod) to paired tagged MRI. Reported circumferential and radial strain ICCs were 0.973 and 0.975~\cite{an2026myonet}. original: A further set of systems is supervised on a downstream label in place of motion. Cine-only infarct delineation used recurrent motion features and optical flow, supervised on manual delineation of delayed-enhancement images~\cite{xu2018}. Deep-learning synthetic strain derived regional wall-motion assessment from cine and was evaluated against the consensus of four cardiothoracic radiologists in 53 patients and 846 segments, reaching an AUC of 0.90 at a 30\% peak radial strain threshold~\cite{masutani2023dlss}. Deep-learning aligned strain was developed to detect fibrotic myocardium in Duchenne muscular dystrophy with LGE as the reference~\cite{koehler2025alignedstrain}, and Bello and colleagues supervised a motion representation directly on survival, reporting a Harrell C index of 0.75 against a human benchmark of 0.59 in 302 patients~\cite{bello2019}. Each is a well-posed study, and in each the supervision target determines what the evidence can support, which in every case is something other than the accuracy of the motion field.
revision: Clinical labels enter these pipelines at different stages. Cine-only infarct delineation combines recurrent motion features and optical flow with manual delayed-enhancement delineations as the target~\cite{xu2018}. DLSS instead learns myocardial velocities and segmentation from registered 4D-flow MRI and derives strain from cine at inference. Its development dataset contained 223 examinations from 219 patients; four-reader consensus wall-motion labels were used for the separate clinical evaluation in 53 patients and 846 segments. The ROC AUC was 0.90; a 30\% peak-radial-strain threshold gave sensitivity 86\% and specificity 85\%~\cite{masutani2023dlss}. Thus the reader labels evaluate the clinical output rather than supervise the motion network.
rationale: 训练信号与临床评价分开，AUC与操作点分开

original: \subsection{What the method record shows by year}
revision:
Deep-learning aligned strain also separates motion estimation from clinical classification. Its cine pipeline detects key phases, segments the myocardium and estimates deformation using image similarity, smoothness and mask agreement; LGE labels the downstream patient-level fibrosis classifier, not the displacement field. Development used 57 patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy, followed by a same-centre temporal holdout of 82 patients. The classification target was the presence of at least one LGE-positive segment, rather than the spatial boundary of fibrosis~\cite{koehler2025alignedstrain}. In a different chamber and population, Bello and colleagues used right-ventricular motion to predict survival in 302 patients with pulmonary hypertension. Internally bootstrap-corrected Harrell C indices were 0.75 for the learned model and 0.59 for a model using manually measured conventional volumetric and functional variables~\cite{bello2019}. Both studies provide clinically relevant discrimination evidence in their tested settings, without converting that evidence into dense motion accuracy or demonstrated treatment benefit.

original: Three patterns in Supplementary Table~S3, plotted by year and family in \cref{fig:timeline}, define the rest of this review. First, the modal evidence across the methods reviewed, and across the 2018--2026 cardiac-specific designs in particular, is agreement between a propagated and a reference segmentation, supplemented by sparse landmark error; by the construction in \cref{fig:same-contours}, that evidence cannot by itself certify material correspondence. Second, where a method is evaluated against a material-sensitive reference, the reference is almost always acquired in a mixed or healthy population, and the comparison is reported as agreement, without error under controlled conditions. Third, the pathology column is mostly ``not reported'': among the estimators reviewed, deliberate evaluation on a focal abnormality of known size and severity appears in one independent synthetic study (\cref{sec:knownmotion}), and the evidence that does exist on pathological hearts tends to be mask agreement or a downstream label. These three patterns describe the published evaluation record; they say nothing about the methods' capability.
revision: Supplementary Table~S3 and \cref{fig:timeline} map selected studies and their reported endpoints. The entries include cine estimators, general registration precedents, tagging-analysis comparators, clinical prediction systems and an evaluation of an existing estimator. They are therefore neither independent cohorts nor a uniform sample of algorithms. Shape and landmark comparisons are common in the cardiac-specific designs, while synthetic motion, DENSE and tagging provide complementary tests in selected studies. Clinical labels add another form of evidence, as the DLSS and aligned-strain examples show. The map records positive endpoints at the available reading depth; an unclassified or unverified endpoint is not counted as an absent experiment. These distinctions, rather than a percentage of the field said to be validated, motivate the target-based synthesis that follows.

original: Within the cine literature retrieved, the most informative single prescribed-focal result is the DeepStrain evaluation reported in the MRXCAT2.0 paper, which is independent of the DeepStrain developers. Four cases were simulated (normal, dilated, hypertrophic and infarcted left ventricles, with ejection fractions of 51\%, 34\%, 41\% and 49\%), and the infarct was modelled as an elliptical free-wall scar. The infarcted ejection fraction stayed at 49\% because remote myocardium compensated for the scar, which is precisely the configuration a global measure cannot see. The prescribed deficit was strongly attribute-dependent before any estimator was applied: ground-truth peak systolic strains were 0.95 (radial), \(-0.18\) (longitudinal) and \(-0.18\) (circumferential) in remote tissue against 0.30, \(-0.17\) and 0.01 in the scar, so radial and circumferential strain are largely abolished inside the scar while longitudinal strain is almost unchanged. Applying DeepStrain gave a mean Dice of 0.82 across phases, lowest for the infarcted case and particularly in the thin scar region, an average displacement error of \(1.0\pm0.9\)~mm, a mean circumferential strain error of \(0.02\pm0.04\) averaged across the four cases, with larger errors in the thinner-walled dilated and infarcted cases, and a general underestimation of radial strain, \(-0.24\pm0.21\) averaged across cases with the lowest performance attributed to the infarcted case at \(-0.20\pm0.21\). All values are case-level averages over mid-ventricular short-axis slices; none is an error measured within the scar region itself~\cite{mrxcat2023}. \Cref{fig:attributes-mrxcat} plots the prescribed deficit and the reported errors side by side.
revision: MRXCAT2.0 provides a useful prescribed-focal example: an evaluation of DeepStrain by a separate development team. Four left-ventricular cases were generated (normal, dilated, hypertrophic and infarcted; ejection fractions 51\%, 34\%, 41\% and 49\%). An elliptical free-wall scar was prescribed in the infarct case, while remote compensation preserved its ejection fraction. The underlying abnormality differed by component: remote-to-scar peak systolic strain changed from 0.95 to 0.30 radially, from \(-0.18\) to 0.01 circumferentially and from \(-0.18\) to \(-0.17\) longitudinally. Radial strain was markedly reduced but retained a substantial residual value; circumferential strain approached zero, while longitudinal strain changed little. These are prescribed tissue values, not errors of the estimator~\cite{mrxcat2023}.
rationale: 区分设定的瘢痕差异和算法误差，撤回唯一性

original: Two qualifications come from the source itself. The authors describe the infarcted case as the worst performer, yet the radial error they report for it (\(-0.20\)) is smaller in magnitude than the across-case average (\(-0.24\)) and the per-case standard deviations overlap, so the ordering rests on the full set of panels and should not be quoted as a quantitative ranking. The experiment also occupies a single point in the space this review is asking about, with one scar geometry, one estimator, mid-ventricular slices only and one simulated signal-to-noise ratio, and the record read does not identify which DeepStrain release or weights were used. What the experiment does establish is the empirical instance of the claim form developed in \cref{sec:threequestions}: on the same images, the same estimator kept the case-averaged circumferential error at \(0.02\pm0.04\) while generally underestimating radial strain, most visibly where the wall was thin. Because the errors are averaged over whole slices, the experiment shows that the circumferential component survived better than the radial component, and it does not report how well the scar itself was localised or bounded. The result is attribute-specific. The single experiment separates none of the candidate explanations for it, which include training-set composition, wall thinning and partial volume in the scar, the generator's image-formation model, and the estimator's own regularisation.
revision:
DeepStrain achieved a reported myocardial Dice of 0.82 across phases and displacement error of \(1.0\pm0.9\)~mm. The reported circumferential strain error was \(0.02\pm0.04\), compared with radial strain error of \(-0.24\pm0.21\) across cases and \(-0.20\pm0.21\) in the infarct case. The source's Figure~14 averages the measures over three mid-ventricular short-axis slices; these summaries do not quantify error within the scar. Although the source describes the infarct case as the lowest performer, its radial mean error is smaller in magnitude than the all-case mean. Neither these means nor overlapping standard deviations establish a uniform case ranking or equivalence. Different metrics can rank cases differently, and the all-case summary includes the infarct case. \Cref{fig:attributes-mrxcat} preserves the reported values while separating them from unmeasured scar attributes.

The generated domain also limits interpretation. The evaluation used one scar geometry and SNR 30, and myocardial texture was removed during image generation. TextNet and DeepStrain both used ACDC data: independence of the evaluating team does not establish independence of the image domain, although shared dataset use alone is not evidence of leakage. The inspected source does not identify the evaluated DeepStrain release or weights. The component-specific errors could reflect image formation, wall thinning and partial volume, training data or estimation constraints; the experiment does not isolate these contributions~\cite{mrxcat2023}.
rationale: 消除SD推断和统一排名；加入生成域及数据独立性边界

original: Known-motion resources answer questions that an in-vivo comparison cannot: whether the representation can express a lesion, whether the optimiser recovers it at a chosen signal-to-noise ratio, and how sampling or regularisation changes magnitude and localisation. Along those lines, resolution has been varied against known motion~\cite{adams2023}, analysis regularisation has been varied against known motion~\cite{barbaroux2025}, and abnormality has been represented in known-motion data~\cite{mrxcat2023,zhou2018straus}. Within the searches recorded here, this review did not identify a study that varied abnormality size, severity or transmurality against known motion while holding the estimator and the measurement definition fixed; that absence is a property of the recorded searches, and it does not assert that no such study exists. The limitation of simulation is just as clear. A simulation is valid only over the anatomy, mechanics, appearance, artefacts and pathology it represents, so passing a phantom test establishes recovery in that regime and leaves in-vivo accuracy open. The appropriate response is to pair simulation with material-sensitive and clinical tests, which the next subsections take up.
revision: Known-motion resources allow investigators to test representation capacity, recovery at a chosen signal-to-noise ratio and sensitivity to sampling or regularisation. Existing work has varied resolution~\cite{adams2023}, varied analysis regularisation~\cite{barbaroux2025}, or represented regional pathology in simulated motion~\cite{mrxcat2023,zhou2018straus}. These are useful precedents for the proposed validation programme. The surviving search records do not establish whether all combinations of graded lesion size, severity, transmurality and fixed-estimator evaluation have already been studied. Here, graded attribute recovery is proposed as a research priority, rather than justified by a claim of field-wide absence. Simulation results remain conditional on the anatomy, mechanics, image formation and pathology represented; paired in-vivo comparisons are needed to assess transfer.
rationale: 保留先例和研究建议，不制造新颖性

original: Recent work continues to show direction- and model-specific success. A 2026 study evaluated one- and two-slice DENSE models and a one-slice cine model using a deforming phantom and 40 healthy volunteers. Circumferential strain was recovered well in the phantom; in volunteers, the one-slice cine model was statistically equivalent to the two-slice DENSE model for endocardial circumferential strain within a prespecified margin of 3.5\% (two one-sided tests) and differed for radial, longitudinal and epicardial circumferential estimates~\cite{jahromi2026densecine}. The result identifies which component, layer and setting were supported and where the slice model was insufficient; it supports neither ``cine works'' nor ``cine fails'' as a general verdict. Selected studies are compared directly in \cref{tab:evidence}.
revision: A 2026 study makes the importance of the endpoint explicit. Jahromi and colleagues compared one- and two-slice DENSE models with a one-slice cine model in a deforming phantom and 40 healthy volunteers. In the volunteer comparison, the endpoint was slice-wise peak median systolic endocardial circumferential strain at two mid-ventricular levels. The cine versus two-slice DENSE mean difference was \(-2.7\) percentage points. Two one-sided tests supported equivalence within a selected margin of \(\pm3.5\) percentage points, despite a significant difference from zero; those are compatible findings because they test different hypotheses. Prospective specification of the margin and the handling of within-person slice correlation were not established by the inspected report. The radial, longitudinal and epicardial circumferential comparisons differed~\cite{jahromi2026densecine}. Thus the result supports a specific healthy, whole-layer comparison, not focal-lesion accuracy or general interchangeability. Selected studies are compared in \cref{tab:evidence}.
rationale: 准确端点、pp单位、selected margin和统计单位不确定性

original: Current evidence most directly supports cine-derived circumferential strain at whole-slice, global and AHA-segment scales when acquisition, software, myocardial layer, reference state and temporal endpoint are matched. Within those bounds, several paired studies found useful agreement with tagging or DENSE, and StrainNet improved end-systolic global and segmental Ecc agreement over the tested conventional feature-tracking pipeline. Scan--rescan and scar/outcome studies add evidence about precision and biological or prognostic relevance. Each of these study types supports use for its stated endpoint, and none converts that endpoint into dense material-motion accuracy.
revision: Routine cine CMR supports useful regional measurements, provided the claim is tied to the measured quantity and validation setting. StrainNet improved end-systolic cine--DENSE agreement over its tested conventional feature-tracking pipeline, while residual limits of agreement and internal validation constrain the inference. Repeatability, scar discrimination and prognosis contribute separate evidence about longitudinal precision and clinical relevance.

original: Support weakens as the requested output becomes more local or changes definition. Radial strain is consistently more product- and method-dependent. Basal/apical, endocardial/transmural, two-/three-dimensional, engineering/Green--Lagrange and end-systolic/peak values cannot be exchanged without qualification. The one independent prescribed-focal test retrieved, DeepStrain on MRXCAT2.0, found a component-specific result (case-averaged circumferential error \(0.02\pm0.04\), radial strain generally underestimated) from one scar geometry, one estimator and slice-averaged endpoints that do not quantify recovery of the scar region itself. In the studies reviewed, direct tests of focal abnormality centroid, lesion-boundary or width error and transmural extent recovery were uncommon or not reported. Timing has been compared mainly at global and segmental level (time to peak between tagging, feature tracking and speckle tracking in 42 participants~\cite{brandt2024}), and focal peak-time error against a material reference remains untested. These are statements about the inspected evidence, and they do not prove that no such work exists. The observed differences in sampling, software and strain definition explain some discordance. Explanations based on information insufficiency, smoothing or low-dimensional bias remain hypotheses until a study varies those factors or measures representation capacity directly.
revision: A claim about a focal abnormality requires evidence at that scale. DeepStrain on MRXCAT2.0 illustrates the distinction: component-specific whole-slice errors were reported in a prescribed-scar setting, but those averages do not quantify recovery inside the scar. Neither a lower mean circumferential error nor a clinically informative label establishes accurate lesion magnitude, boundary or timing. Apparent disagreement across studies can reflect software, sampling, strain convention, statistical unit and reference uncertainty, as well as estimation error; controlled comparisons are needed before attributing it to information loss or regularisation.

original: A defensible regional claim should therefore name the acquisition, input, estimator, population, spatial unit, myocardial layer, reference state, time point, comparator and tolerance. Known-motion resources such as STRAUS and MRXCAT2.0 can test capacity and estimator error; CMAC contributes sparse cross-modality correspondence; and paired human cine--DENSE/tagging resources such as Stanford can test transfer once explicit processing and alignment are done. Combining these complementary tests with participant-aware statistics and downstream clinical evaluation can identify where routine cine CMR preserves abnormality magnitude, location, extent and timing, and where the appropriate conclusion remains unresolved.
revision: The practical requirement is a measurement contract linking acquisition, estimator, population, spatial unit, strain definition, time point, comparator and tolerance. Known-motion tests can probe representation and recovery; paired cine--DENSE or tagging comparisons can assess in-vivo agreement; tissue and outcome studies can test clinical relevance. Combining these complementary designs with participant-aware statistics offers a way to determine which abnormality attributes routine cine preserves and which remain unresolved, without asking a single validation target to establish them all.

original: \caption{Two-track evidence map for regional strain from routine cine CMR. (a) Estimation track. Cine supplies image cues (blood--myocardium borders, weak intramural texture, time) without a material label; an estimator infers material correspondence from them, and because the data term alone does not identify the map, the prior \(\alpha\mathcal R\) selects among candidates; strain is then fixed by convention through eight specifications (01 reference, 02 measure, 03 axes and sign, 04 layer and dimension, 05 derivative and smoothing, 06 region, 07 temporal readout, 08 aggregation order). The readouts beside the segmental curves are computed from the drawn curves for the reduced segment (11): one curve gives \(-0.01\) at end-systole, \(-0.08\) at the systolic peak and \(-0.12\) at the post-systolic peak, and the minimum of the segment-mean curve (\(-0.16\)) differs from the mean of the segment minima (\(-0.18\)). Circled letters mark three failure points, each testable on its own: input sufficiency (I), by re-imaging the same motion more finely; estimation (E), by varying the regularisation weight \(\alpha\) with the images fixed; representation (R), by projecting the known field onto the estimator's basis. (b) Validation track. Each reference supports one claim and leaves the next open on its own: known motion (the MRXCAT2.0 test of DeepStrain; errors are slice-level means, \cref{fig:attributes-mrxcat}), paired DENSE or tagging (vendor range of cine feature-tracking ICC against tagging; DENSE against tagging; StrainNet against conventional feature tracking with a DENSE reference), precision (REGAIN against GRAPPA limits of agreement; Strain-8 scan--rescan), tissue characterisation (segment-level discrimination of LGE \(>50\%\) transmural scar) and outcome or reader labels (survival C-index; wall-motion abnormality AUC against a four-reader consensus). Values are as reported in the cited studies and in \cref{tab:evidence} and \cref{tab:attributes}; they are not pooled because the quantities differ. Panel a is a conceptual schematic without study data. Programmatic schematic or numerical redraw; sources and preparation are stated in the declarations.}
revision: \caption{From image cues to a regional measurement. (a) Conceptual estimation chain: cine supplies anatomical and intensity cues; correspondence is inferred; strain and its regional readout depend on the stated definition. The registration objective is one example, not a universal training loss. The reduced segment is 11. Curve-derived readouts are \(-0.01\) at end-systole, \(-0.08\) at the systolic peak and \(-0.12\) at the post-systolic peak; minimum of the mean curve (\(-0.16\)) differs from mean of segment minima (\(-0.18\)). Input (I), estimation (E) and representation (R) tests probe potentially coupled error sources. (b) Selected empirical endpoints, not a pooled ranking. MRXCAT2.0 values are slice averages~\cite{mrxcat2023}; Militaru LS/CS ICCs compare FT with tagging, whereas its RS range compares FT vendors~\cite{militaru2021}. Cao compares DENSE with tagging~\cite{cao2018}; StrainNet compares cine-derived Ecc with DENSE~\cite{wang2023strainnet}. REGAIN limits describe reconstruction-plus-analysis agreement~\cite{yoon2023regain}, while Strain-8 assesses repeatability~\cite{bell2025strain8}. Kihlberg's ROC endpoint is end-systolic segmental Ecc versus high-transmurality LGE~\cite{kihlberg2020clinical}. Bello's internally corrected C index concerns RV-based survival prediction in pulmonary hypertension~\cite{bello2019}; DLSS AUC concerns reader-defined wall-motion abnormality, separately from its operating threshold~\cite{masutani2023dlss}. Panel a is calculated illustration; panel b redraws published numbers.}

original: \caption{From image cues to a regional measurement. (a) Conceptual estimation chain: cine supplies anatomical and intensity cues; correspondence is inferred; strain and its regional readout depend on the stated definition. The registration objective is one example, not a universal training loss. The reduced segment is 11. Curve-derived readouts are \(-0.01\) at end-systole, \(-0.08\) at the systolic peak and \(-0.12\) at the post-systolic peak; minimum of the mean curve (\(-0.16\)) differs from mean of segment minima (\(-0.18\)). Input (I), estimation (E) and representation (R) tests probe potentially coupled error sources. (b) Selected empirical endpoints, not a pooled ranking. MRXCAT2.0 values are slice averages~\cite{mrxcat2023}; Militaru LS/CS ICCs compare FT with tagging, whereas its RS range compares FT vendors~\cite{militaru2021}. Cao compares DENSE with tagging~\cite{cao2018}; StrainNet compares cine-derived Ecc with DENSE~\cite{wang2023strainnet}. REGAIN limits describe reconstruction-plus-analysis agreement~\cite{yoon2023regain}, while Strain-8 assesses repeatability~\cite{bell2025strain8}. Kihlberg's ROC endpoint is end-systolic segmental Ecc versus high-transmurality LGE~\cite{kihlberg2020clinical}. Bello's internally corrected C index concerns RV-based survival prediction in pulmonary hypertension~\cite{bello2019}; DLSS AUC concerns reader-defined wall-motion abnormality, separately from its operating threshold~\cite{masutani2023dlss}. Panel a is calculated illustration; panel b redraws published numbers.}
revision: \caption{From image cues to a regional measurement. (a) Conceptual chain: correspondence is inferred and strain depends on the measurement definition. The registration objective is an example, not a universal loss. Segment~11 is reduced; all curve readouts are calculated illustrations. Input (I), estimation (E) and representation (R) tests probe potentially coupled errors. (b) Selected empirical endpoints, not a pooled ranking. MRXCAT2.0 reports slice averages~\cite{mrxcat2023}. Militaru LS/CS ICCs compare FT with tagging; its RS range compares FT vendors~\cite{militaru2021}. Cao reports mid-slice peak Ecc~\cite{cao2018}; StrainNet reports end-systolic cine--DENSE Ecc agreement~\cite{wang2023strainnet}. REGAIN assesses reconstruction-plus-analysis agreement~\cite{yoon2023regain}; Strain-8 assesses repeatability~\cite{bell2025strain8}. Kihlberg's ROC uses end-systolic segmental Ecc and LGE~\cite{kihlberg2020clinical}. Bello's corrected C index concerns RV survival prediction in pulmonary hypertension~\cite{bello2019}; DLSS AUC evaluates reader-defined wall-motion abnormality across thresholds~\cite{masutani2023dlss}. The axis value 0.5 is a scale reference, not an observed result.}
